newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-Ansett,Air NZ,SIA seal potent link.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ansett,Air NZ,SIA seal potent link.

text.p: Australian airline Ansett and Air New Zealand on Friday announced plans to cement an alliance with one of Asia's most successful carriers, Singapore Airlines, (SIA) in a move aimed at giving the three a competitive edge.

The three airlines, and Ansett's fledgling Asian operation Ansett International, said they planned to share capacity and use their new economy of scale to implement joint purchasing, promotion and cargo operations.
The alliance, said to be the largest based in the Asia-Pacific, boasts coverage of over 200 cities in 47 countries, operating a combined fleet of 223 aircraft.

"A good small airline in an increasing liberal world will find it increasingly difficult to compete with a good big airline," Ansett chief, Rod Eddington told a news conference held by the three carriers to announce the deal.
"Smaller airlines particularly will be looking to form alliances like the one we are forming today," Eddington said.

Ansett, jointly owned by Air New Zealand and News Corp Ltd, is the weakest financially of the alliance partners and such a tie-up is seen as crucial if Ansett is to get its bottom line airborne over the next three years.
The announcement followed weeks of speculation about such an alliance, but stopped short of an expected equity partnership.
The airlines' representatives refused to speculate about a possible future equity deal.

The benefits of the alliance were less clear for SIA but analysts said the airline could be positioning itself to get better access to Australia's profitable but tightly-held domestic aviation market.
SIA chief executive Cheong Choong Kong told reporters on Friday that the airline had no immediate plans to operate in either the Australian or New Zealand domestic markets.
But he said SIA wanted more exposure to Australia's local airline market.
"This alliance actually gives us the confidence to expand further into Australia," Cheong said.
The manager of Ansett's international operations, Greg Wallace, said the alliance deal would not exclude the three carriers from pursuing links with other airlines.
Air New Zealand's chief Jim McCrea said the alliance would not hinder his carrier's ambition to join the recently formed Star alliance between six international airlines.
"We are progressively forming partnerships with members of the Star Alliance and that is not incompatable with the Singapore, Ansett, Ansett International alliance," he said.
Ansett's Eddington said the memorandum of understanding the three airlines had signed was not the final contract but committed the three to negotiating the alliance.

"Such an alliance will need approval from the appropriate regulators but we are confident that we can demonstrate to these regulators that our proposed joint activity will provide tangible benefits to the travelling public," he said.
Air New Zealand's McCrea said the carrier would shortly start code-sharing with Singapore Airlines if given approval from New Zealand's ministry of transport.
